problem: A candidate retrieval service died before a paid 25-question arm, yet the old runner treated 200 failed search transports plus terminal prose as 25 successful research runs. This both invalidated the comparison and spent provider budget on evidence-free executions.
simplest_baseline: Before each provider subprocess, require a healthy search endpoint with the exact frozen retriever identity; if a transport failure occurs mid-run, mark that run failed and abort the remaining batch instead of adding retries, agents, or a workflow framework.
hypothesis: A fail-closed tool boundary will prevent provider launch when retrieval is unavailable or identity-drifted, mark any mid-run search/open transport error as a failed execution, and leave both retrievers usable after a zero-provider live smoke.
changed_mechanisms: fail-closed search-service identity preflight, terminal tool-error status, and batch abort
anti_claim: This is an execution-integrity repair. It does not improve the frozen model, retrieval quality, answer accuracy, or benchmark standing.

framework_comparisons.current_gap: Checkpointing is useful only after dependency health is explicit; more isolated workers would multiply calls against the same dead retriever.
Runtime configurability does not by itself prevent a terminal answer from being accepted after every evidence tool failed; the smaller missing boundary is fail-closed dependency validation.
Crawler breadth cannot make an evidence-free run valid when the tool transport is unavailable; health and failure semantics must precede concurrency.
Graph fan-out would amplify a shared search outage, so dependency identity and batch-stop semantics are the prerequisite rather than another search node.

frozen_controls: same 8768 baseline and 8769 candidate retriever identities
same v10 and v14 research budgets
only execution-status and preflight behavior may change
next_action: Keep the invalid repeat grid closed, preserve the restored named services, and preregister a new clean effectiveness experiment whose runner and retriever hashes include the accepted fail-closed boundary.
claim_boundary: Passing this loop means only that dependency identity, tool-error status, batch abort, and local search/open availability are verified without paid calls. It does not restore, score, or reinterpret the invalid trial-3 candidate arm.
